note: Language Access has no config UI (configure=null) and no config of its own. Its entire control surface is a dynamic permission set 'access language <langcode>' (one per configured language, built by LanguageAccessPermissions::permissions() from the language manager). hook_install grants 'access language <default>' to the anonymous and authenticated roles. Enforcement: a kernel.request subscriber throws 403 for the current language when the permission is missing, plus hooks strip the language from switch links, hreflang tags, simple_sitemap links, user-form/language_select options, browser negotiation, config_pages context, and the content-translation overview. Medium/hard cases add a throwaway language (namespaced langcode) and grant/deny 'access language <lang>' on namespaced roles, verified by reading role permissions.

evals.prompt: The language_access module for Drupal restricts who can view each site language. What is the machine-name format of the permission it provides to control access to a language, and how many such permissions exist relative to the site's languages?
evals.expected_output: It provides one dynamic permission per configured language named 'access language <langcode>' (e.g. 'access language en', 'access language fr'), generated by LanguageAccessPermissions::permissions() from the language manager. There is exactly one such permission for each configured language.

evals.prompt: I enabled language_access on a Drupal 11 site but there is no settings/configure page for it. How do I grant a role access to a specific language, and what happens to a user who lacks that permission when they open a page in that language?
evals.expected_output: There is no config UI (configure=null). You grant the 'access language <langcode>' permission per role on People -> Permissions (/admin/people/permissions). A user lacking the permission for the current request's language gets an HTTP 403 (AccessDeniedHttpException), thrown by LanguageAccessSubscriber on the kernel.request event.

evals.prompt: Apart from returning 403 on a blocked language's pages, what else does language_access do to a language the current user cannot access - in the language switcher, hreflang alternate tags, and a Simple Sitemap - and does the block apply to Drush/CLI?
evals.expected_output: It removes inaccessible languages from the language switcher (hook_language_switch_links_alter), strips their rel=alternate hreflang tags (hook_page_attachments_alter), drops them from simple_sitemap links (hook_simple_sitemap_links_alter), and limits user-form / language_select options. The 403 block is skipped on CLI (PHP_SAPI === 'cli'), so Drush and cron are unaffected.

evals.prompt: This Drupal site uses language_access. A non-default language has been added and exactly one custom role has been granted access to it. Inspect the live site and give the machine name of the role that was granted access to the Icelandic (is) language.
evals.expected_output: The role machine name is langaccess_reviewer: its user.role.langaccess_reviewer config lists the permission 'access language is'.

evals.prompt: The Norwegian Bokmal (nb) language has been added to this site and two custom roles exist, langaccess_alpha and langaccess_beta. Exactly one of them has been granted the language_access permission to access nb. Inspect the live role permissions and state which role can access the nb language.
evals.expected_output: langaccess_beta has the 'access language nb' permission; langaccess_alpha does not. Check user.role.langaccess_beta / user.role.langaccess_alpha permissions.

evals.prompt: This site has the Faroese (fo) language enabled and a custom role 'langaccess_task' that currently cannot access it. Using the language_access module's permission model, grant the langaccess_task role access to the Faroese (fo) language, and apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Grant the 'access language fo' permission to the langaccess_task role (e.g. Role::load('langaccess_task')->grantPermission('access language fo')->save(), or drush role:perm:add langaccess_task 'access language fo', or via /admin/people/permissions).

evals.prompt: The Western Frisian (fy) language is enabled on this site but anonymous visitors currently get access denied when they open Frisian pages. Make it so anonymous (not-logged-in) visitors are allowed to view the Frisian (fy) language, using the language_access module. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Grant the 'access language fy' permission to the anonymous role (user.role.anonymous), e.g. Role::load('anonymous')->grantPermission('access language fy')->save() or drush role:perm:add anonymous 'access language fy'.
